channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Meta Releases Open AI Model While Keeping Its Best Tech Closed
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. made one of its new artificial intelligence models available for developers to download and modify, while keeping its most advanced technology closed in an effort to convert its AI investments into revenue.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion in Q3 Before IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, and the company achieved profitability in the quarter on an adjusted basis. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave’s Selloff Is ‘Buying Opportunity,’ Deutsche Bank Says
item.description: The bruising selloff in CoreWeave Inc. shares this week has wiped out more than $10 billion in market value in just four sessions due to the company’s deteriorating credit profile.
item.dc:creator: Subrat Patnaik

item.title: Apple HomeView Is Finally Here + Touchscreen MacBook Pro Launch Details
item.description:
In this episode of Power On, Mark Gurman is joined by Bloomberg’s Chris Welch and Vlad Savov to break down Apple’s long-awaited smart home launch. Plus, Mark reveals new details about Apple’s upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro launch, including plans for a late-October event in Los Angeles, a potential November release date and what to expect from the OLED iPad mini.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sony Debuts $5,900 Gold-Plated Walkman Music Player for Enthusiasts
item.description: Sony Group Corp. introduced a trio of premium digital music players priced from $1,900 to $5,900, marking the first new hardware in several years carrying the storied Walkman name.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: Telefónica Is Said to Offer Buyer Loan to Rescue Mexico Deal
item.description: Telefónica SA is considering granting a vendor loan to the buyer of its Mexican unit to help complete a deal that was announced in April, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga, Rodrigo Orihuela and Michael O'Boyle

item.title: CityFibre Asks Banks to Restructure Debt and Fund New M&A Deals
item.description: Cityfibre Infrastructure Holdings Ltd. has asked banks to write down part of a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) loan and to provide new money for acquisitions as the UK fiber company seeks to stay afloat, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Paula Doenecke and Constantine Courcoulas

item.title: Nvidia CEO Says There’s No Need to Backstop Troubled CoreWeave
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang pushed back on financial concerns about troubled CoreWeave Inc., one of his key customers, and said he doesn’t think the AI data center operator will need a bailout from his company.
item.dc:creator: Charles Daly and Ian King

item.title: Ryan Israel on Investing Beyond AI
item.description: As AI stocks retreat and rates remain a concern, Pershing Square CIO Ryan Israel joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why the firm is focused on durable businesses at attractive prices. He discusses the long-term cases for the eye-care company Alcon and Netflix, when a macro bet makes sense and the firm’s expansion into private growth companies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Credit Risk Hits Record as Default Odds Top 60% on Borrowing Plans
item.description: A measure of CoreWeave Inc.’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as its high-yield bonds extended declines, rattled by the AI cloud-computing company’s talk of tapping vast pools of capital from insurers.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua

item.title: Anthropic Urged to Pause IPO for AI Safety by NYC Comptroller
item.description: Anthropic should pause its initial public offering until it has fully addressed risks around artificial intelligence, according to New York City’s comptroller. A letter from Mark Levine addressed to Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei on Wednesday suggested the Claude developer should instead focus on addressing the unprecedented risks of the technology. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Santander's Ana Botin on US Growth, Debt, AI and the Global Economy | The David Rubenstein Show
item.description: Santander Executive Chair Ana Botin sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss the bank's expansion in the US, including its recent acquisition of Webster Financial, and why she sees lack of economic growth as one of the biggest challenges facing the global economy. She also discusses US debt, the outlook for the US and European economies amid geopolitical uncertainty, and the impact of AI on banking and jobs. Botin is on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This episode was recorded July 13 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Traders Are Already Betting on Ambani’s Big Jio IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms Ltd.’s record-breaking upcoming initial public offering is already trading on crypto rails, giving investors a round-the-clock venue to bet on the company’s valuation even before its shares hit local Indian exchanges.
item.dc:creator: Sidhartha Shukla

item.title: Dangote Cement Adds Goldman, UBS for November London Listing
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc added Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and UBS Group AG as bookrunners for a London listing that it’s preparing as soon as November, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Laura Gardner Cuesta, Loni Prinsloo, Anthony Osae-Brown and Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro

item.title: Ripple Opens $9 Billion Perps Boom to Wall Street Clients
item.description: Cryptocurrency firms are increasingly turning to the world of traditional finance for their next leg of growth by positioning themselves as competitors to Wall Street’s entrenched institutional businesses.
item.dc:creator: Yiqin Shen and Muyao Shen

item.title: Taiwan Blocks Coinbase, Kalshi Over Suspected Election Bets
item.description: Taiwan has blocked the websites of Coinbase Global Inc. and Kalshi Inc. over suspected election betting, weeks before local polls that will test support for President Lai Ching-te’s government.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: Israeli Firms Put Spyware at Al Jazeera via Ads, Report Says
item.description: Two Israeli companies manipulated online advertisements to install surveillance software on dozens of computers at the Qatari news organization Al Jazeera, researchers have found.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: SpaceX’s Spectrum Purchase Exposes Risks for Big Telecom Stocks
item.description: Telecom stocks have long been considered a relatively safe bet for investors, offering predictable growth, limited downside and healthy dividends. But a combination of competition from SpaceX and rising Treasury yields is threatening to upend that equation.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion in Quarter Before IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence company pushes ahead with plans to go public.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Natasha Mascarenhas, Rebecca Torrence and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Rocket Lab Falls After Neutron Rocket Debut Delayed to 2027
item.description: Rocket Lab Corp. shares plunged after the company again delayed the debut of its more powerful Neutron rocket, pushing the vehicle’s first flight to 2027.
item.dc:creator: Loren Grush
